title: Rig Project config (rig.yaml)
description: Committed Project intent: identity, Services, Tools, routes and Target patches, in format rig/v2. A rig.yaml without format is rig/v1, described by rig-v1.schema.json; rig config upgrade rewrites it to rig/v2.

format.description: The rig.yaml format this file is written in. rig/v2 is the current format. A file without format is rig/v1, which Rig still reads and warns about; rig config upgrade rewrites a file to the current format.

production_branch.description: Branch whose pushes deploy the Stable Target; defaults to the Host deploy.production_branch, then main.

domain.description: Stable Target hostname. Previews default to <preview-name>.<domain>; the Working copy has no hostname unless its patch sets one. ${rig.target} is the only reference a hostname may contain.

supervisor.description: Process supervisor: rigd (child processes owned by the daemon) or launchd (per-Service launchd agents). The Project sets it for all its Services. It can also be set per Target role under targets.<role>.supervisor.

build.description: Shared shell build command, run once in the workspace before any Service or Tool build. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}. A Service's env is not available here.

build_timeout.description: Duration budget for the shared build and the default for Service and Tool builds (default 10m).

env.description: Public environment values passed to the process; never put secrets here. Values may use ${...} references. Bind-style keys such as HOST or BIND_ADDR may not use a wildcard address.

additionalProperties.description: Public value. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

env_file.description: Environment file path, or an ordered list of paths where later files win. Listed files are required and hold plain KEY=value data; their contents never take part in ${...} references. Relative paths resolve against the workspace; ~ is the operator home. The path itself may use references. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

propertyNames.description: Service or Tool name used in references, dependencies and output.

run.description: Foreground shell command run with /bin/sh -c; explicit bindings must be localhost only. Referenced values with spaces or shell characters are single-quoted unless the reference is already quoted. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

build.description: Shell build command of this Service, run with /bin/sh -c in the workspace during preparation, never as a start hook; explicit bindings must be localhost only. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

build_timeout.description: Build duration budget such as 10m; a build past it is terminated and recorded as failed, never as completed.

ports.description: Named local TCP ports: auto lets Rig choose and keep a free port, a number from 1 to 65535 pins it. Previews always use chosen ports.

check.description: Local HTTP URL or shell command that passes when the Service is healthy: an HTTP URL must answer with a status below 400 (a redirect is not followed), a command must exit 0. Referenced values in a shell command are quoted as in run. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

start_timeout.description: How long the Service may take to pass its check when it starts, or without one to accept a connection on every declared port, such as 30s (the default).

interval.description: How often Rig runs health.check while the Service runs, such as 30s (at least 5s). Without it the check runs only at start. Checks begin one interval after the start check passed, pause while the Service is starting or stopping, and never overlap.

timeout.description: How long one ongoing check may take before it counts as failed, such as 5s (the default). Needs health.interval; the start check is bounded by start_timeout instead.

failures.description: Failed ongoing checks in a row before Rig marks the Service unhealthy and acts, from 1 to 100 (default 3). Needs health.interval.

on_failure.description: What Rig does once the Service is marked unhealthy: report (the default) shows it unhealthy in status and Activity, and a Stable Target counts as down; restart stops it through the normal stop path, within its stop_timeout, and starts it again, waiting about 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, then an hour between restarts while it stays unhealthy. Health restarts do not use the automatic restart budget. Needs health.interval.

retry_for.description: With on_failure: restart, how long Rig keeps restarting a Service that stays unhealthy, such as 6h. After that Rig leaves it as it is, reports it unhealthy and says in status that it gave up. Omitted, Rig never gives up.

health.description: How Rig checks this Service. health.check must pass before the Service counts as started and before a Service that depends on it starts. Without a check Rig waits for every declared port to accept a connection. With health.interval Rig keeps checking while it runs.

stop_timeout.description: How long the Service may take to exit after its stop signal (SIGTERM) before Rig ends it with SIGKILL, such as 2m (default 10s, at most 1h). Every stop waits for it: rig down, rig restart, a deploy that replaces or rolls back the Target, a Preview destroy, and the stop of a failed start. rig down --kill skips it.

depends_on.description: Services that must be running and ready before this one starts; a later dependency failure does not restart this Service.

items.description: Service or Tool name used in references, dependencies and output.

restart.description: Automatic restart after a known exit: always (default), on-failure, or no. An explicit up or restart starts the Service under every policy.

tools.description: Installed command-line Tools keyed by name.

propertyNames.description: Service or Tool name used in references, dependencies and output.

bin.description: Executable path relative to the workspace; published in <RIG_ROOT>/bin under the Tool name for the Stable Target and <tool>-<target> elsewhere. An executable is copied there and runs from there, so it must be self-contained, like a compiled binary, or name the checkout it needs itself: dirname "$0" is <RIG_ROOT>/bin. A source file (.ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs) is not copied; it is published as a shim that runs it in place with the bun rigd install recorded, so its relative imports resolve. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

additionalProperties.description: Upstream of this prefix: exactly one ${services.<service>.ports.<port>} reference to a declared port, such as ${services.web.ports.http}. No other reference or text is allowed.

proxy.description: Path prefix to declared port reference. Prefixes match at a slash boundary, longest first, and the upstream path is unchanged; '/' is required.

targets.description: Role-keyed Target names and settings patches: working, stable and the preview template.

working.description: Working copy Target name and settings patch.

name.description: Name that selects and displays the Working copy Target (default local). Renaming keeps its identity and stored data.

domain.description: Hostname for this role's Targets, such as ${rig.target}.preview.app.test. ${rig.target} is the only reference a hostname may contain.

check.description: Local HTTP URL or shell command that passes when the Service is healthy: an HTTP URL must answer with a status below 400 (a redirect is not followed), a command must exit 0. Referenced values in a shell command are quoted as in run. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

start_timeout.description: How long the Service may take to pass its check when it starts, or without one to accept a connection on every declared port, such as 30s (the default).

interval.description: How often Rig runs health.check while the Service runs, such as 30s (at least 5s). Without it the check runs only at start. Checks begin one interval after the start check passed, pause while the Service is starting or stopping, and never overlap.

timeout.description: How long one ongoing check may take before it counts as failed, such as 5s (the default). Needs health.interval; the start check is bounded by start_timeout instead.

failures.description: Failed ongoing checks in a row before Rig marks the Service unhealthy and acts, from 1 to 100 (default 3). Needs health.interval.

on_failure.description: What Rig does once the Service is marked unhealthy: report (the default) shows it unhealthy in status and Activity, and a Stable Target counts as down; restart stops it through the normal stop path, within its stop_timeout, and starts it again, waiting about 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, then an hour between restarts while it stays unhealthy. Health restarts do not use the automatic restart budget. Needs health.interval.

retry_for.description: With on_failure: restart, how long Rig keeps restarting a Service that stays unhealthy, such as 6h. After that Rig leaves it as it is, reports it unhealthy and says in status that it gave up. Omitted, Rig never gives up.

health.description: How Rig checks this Service. health.check must pass before the Service counts as started and before a Service that depends on it starts. Without a check Rig waits for every declared port to accept a connection. With health.interval Rig keeps checking while it runs.

stop_timeout.description: How long the Service may take to exit after its stop signal (SIGTERM) before Rig ends it with SIGKILL, such as 2m (default 10s, at most 1h). Every stop waits for it: rig down, rig restart, a deploy that replaces or rolls back the Target, a Preview destroy, and the stop of a failed start. rig down --kill skips it.

depends_on.description: Services that must be running and ready before this one starts; a later dependency failure does not restart this Service.

items.description: Service or Tool name used in references, dependencies and output.

restart.description: Automatic restart after a known exit: always (default), on-failure, or no. An explicit up or restart starts the Service under every policy.

env.description: Public environment values passed to the process; never put secrets here. Values may use ${...} references. Bind-style keys such as HOST or BIND_ADDR may not use a wildcard address.

additionalProperties.description: Public value. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

env_file.description: Environment file path, or an ordered list of paths where later files win. Listed files are required and hold plain KEY=value data; their contents never take part in ${...} references. Relative paths resolve against the workspace; ~ is the operator home. The path itself may use references. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}, ${rig.data}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.

tools.description: Setting overrides keyed by an existing Tool name; a patch cannot add or remove Tools.

propertyNames.description: Service or Tool name used in references, dependencies and output.

build.description: Shell build command run with /bin/sh -c in the workspace during preparation, never as a start hook; explicit bindings must be localhost only. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}. A Service's env is not available here.

build_timeout.description: Build duration budget such as 10m; a build past it is terminated and recorded as failed, never as completed.

bin.description: Executable path relative to the workspace; published in <RIG_ROOT>/bin under the Tool name for the Stable Target and <tool>-<target> elsewhere. An executable is copied there and runs from there, so it must be self-contained, like a compiled binary, or name the checkout it needs itself: dirname "$0" is <RIG_ROOT>/bin. A source file (.ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs) is not copied; it is published as a shim that runs it in place with the bun rigd install recorded, so its relative imports resolve. References: ${env.NAME}, ${services.<service>.ports.<port>}, a scalar setting by its path such as ${services.api.stop_timeout}, ${rig.target}, ${rig.workspace}, ${rig.host}, ${rig.url}. $${VAR} writes a literal ${VAR}.
